title: Foot and Ankle Sports Injuries: Diagnosis, Treatment, and Contemporary Orthopedic Innovations for the General Practitioner.

sections.label: UNLABELED
sections.text: General practitioners (GPs) are frequently the first clinicians to evaluate athletic and nonathletic foot and ankle injuries. Six common foot and ankle conditions seen by GPs are Achilles tendon injuries, lateral ankle ligament sprains, plantar plate injuries/turf toe, ankle fractures and syndesmotic injuries, Lisfranc injuries, and fifth metatarsal base fractures. For each condition, this review outlines clinical diagnostic features, appropriate use of imaging, and decision making regarding conservative management strategies versus surgery. Nonoperative management initiated by GPs include functional bracing, protected weight bearing, activity modification, and structured rehabilitation protocols. Indications for orthopedic referral, such as failure of conservative management, mechanical instability or joint laxity on examination, radiographic evidence of displacement or unstable fracture, high-grade ligamentous or plantar plate disruption, and involvement of high-demand athletes, also are reviewed. By understanding common patient presentations, appropriate initial management, and indications for referral to orthopedic specialists, GPs can optimize early care, reduce diagnostic delay, and improve long-term functional outcomes for patients with foot and ankle sports injuries.
